description: A composite of six TEM micrographs — (a), (b), (d), (e), (f) bright-field images and (c) a fine-scale speckled image — each carrying a printed scale bar and a panel letter, documenting the deformation substructure of two austenitic low-density steels strained to a tensile strain of 0.15. (a) 1 µm bar: two sets of intersecting parallel slip bands forming a near-orthogonal grid inside a γ grain of 28Mn0Ni, with dense dislocation tangles at the upper left. (b) 1 µm bar: closely spaced parallel slip bands cut by a single dark diagonal band — the slip band–annealing twin interaction in the same alloy. (c) 200 nm bar: speckled contrast containing many nm-scale particles together with brighter elongated features, imaged where κ-carbide shearing occurs in 15Mn5Ni. (d) 2 µm bar: sparsely and inhomogeneously spaced slip bands crossing a large grain in 15Mn5Ni. (e) 1 µm bar: tangled dislocation networks/cells concentrated around a dark B2 particle. (f) 5 µm bar: red arrows mark sparse thin parallel lamellae identified as deformation twins in γ grains. Collectively the panels argue that 28Mn0Ni deforms by fine, homogeneous planar glide whereas 15Mn5Ni shows coarser bands plus κ-carbide shearing and B2 pile-up. No numerical values other than scale-bar lengths and panel letters are printed on the panels.

subfigures.description: Bright-field TEM micrograph, 1 µm scale bar, of 28Mn0Ni γ grain. Two sets of intersecting parallel slip bands form a near-orthogonal grid pattern; dense tangled dislocations concentrate in the upper-left corner.
Bright-field TEM micrograph, 1 µm scale bar, of 28Mn0Ni. Closely spaced parallel slip bands traversed by a single dark diagonal band, consistent with slip band–annealing twin interaction.

Fine-scale micrograph (dark-speckled contrast), 200 nm scale bar, of 15Mn5Ni. Many nm-scale particles plus brighter elongated features are visible, consistent with κ-carbide shearing; individual particle sizes cannot be measured at this resolution.
Bright-field TEM micrograph, 2 µm scale bar, of 15Mn5Ni. Parallel slip bands spaced widely and inhomogeneously across a large grain, with a few faint bands crossing near-perpendicularly.
Bright-field TEM micrograph, 1 µm scale bar. Dense tangled dislocation networks forming cell-like arrangements concentrated around a dark, blocky particle (B2) near the bottom of the field of view.
Bright-field TEM micrograph, 5 µm scale bar. Several red arrows point to thin parallel lamellae/bands inside grains, identified in the caption as sparse deformation twins.

observations.observation: Panel (a) shows intersecting slip bands forming a near-orthogonal grid of two glide-plane families in a γ grain, with a heavily tangled dislocation region at the upper left; scale bar = 1 µm.
Panel (b) shows closely spaced parallel slip bands crossed by a single dark diagonal band; scale bar = 1 µm.
Panel (c) uses a 200 nm scale bar, the finest in the group, and shows a speckled distribution of nm-scale particles with brighter elongated features.
Panel (d) uses a 2 µm scale bar and shows slip bands that are widely and heterogeneously spaced compared with panels (a) and (b).
Panel (e) shows tangled dislocation networks/cells localised around a dark blocky particle; scale bar = 1 µm.
Panel (f) uses a 5 µm scale bar and carries red arrows marking thin parallel lamellae; no other annotation or numeric label is printed.

The caption states the panels are TEM micrographs of (a) slip bands and (b) slip band–annealing twin interaction in 28Mn0Ni alloy, and (c) shearing of κ-carbides, (d) slip band, (e) dislocation pile up around B2 and (f) deformation twins in few γ grains in 15Mn5Ni alloy.
The caption states the samples were deformed to a tensile strain of 0.15.
The citing text reports the average slip band spacing as ∼100–200 nm in 28Mn0Ni versus ∼400–600 nm in 15Mn5Ni; neither value is printed in the figure.
The citing text states slip band spacing was relatively inhomogeneous in 15Mn5Ni, and that the bands are homogeneously distributed in 28Mn0Ni.
The citing text states the 15Mn5Ni alloy showed sparse deformation twins (arrowed in Fig. 8f) which were absent in the 28Mn0Ni alloy.
The citing text interprets the deformation structure of both alloys as pronounced planar dislocation glide with slip bands being crystallographic glide planes of high dislocation density.
The caption's Greek symbols are rendered as '??' in the supplied text, so the alloy phase names (κ-carbide, γ grain) are reconstructed from context rather than read directly from the caption string.

unreadable_items: Panel (c): individual κ-carbide particle sizes and any size distribution cannot be resolved or measured at the supplied resolution
Panels: no crystallographic indices, diffraction patterns or beam-direction labels are printed, so grain orientations cannot be determined from the images
Exact number of red arrows and their precise target lamellae in (f) is only partially resolvable
